findings.title: Working-hours end uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
findings.body: In the new working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable`, `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — the same value as `start`. It should be `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`. Consequence: the `end > workingHour.endTime` half of the condition can never trigger, so a slot that starts inside working hours but whose end spills past `workingHour.endTime` (e.g. working hours 09:00–17:00, slot 16:30–17:30) is incorrectly treated as inside working hours. With a 60-minute event this can return bookable slots that extend past the organizer's day.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === instead of isSame
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly-constructed Dayjs objects with strict equality. Dayjs objects are compared by reference, so this branch is unreachable. The intent appears to be "override has zero duration / is empty", which should be `…isSame(…)`. Consequence: an empty/zero-length date override is never short-circuited and the surrounding code falls through to the other boundary checks, which can produce wrong availability when start and end coincide.

findings.title: Working-hours day/hour/minute read from UTC, not organizer tz
findings.body: `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`, so `slotStartTime.day()`, `.hour()` and `.minute()` return UTC values, while `workingHours` are stored in the organizer's timezone. The membership check `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` and the minute comparison will be wrong near day boundaries or for organizers not in UTC (e.g. a slot at 23:30 IST = 18:00 UTC will be checked against the UTC day/hour instead of the IST day/hour). This can return slots outside the organizer's working day or filter out slots that should be available.

findings.title: Date-override day match is compared in UTC, not organizer tz
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` compares two UTC-formatted dates. The date override is a calendar day in the organizer's timezone, and `slotStartTime` is in UTC. Around the day boundary (e.g. override on 2024-01-01 IST = 2023-12-31 18:30 UTC …) a slot on the correct local day can be compared against the wrong UTC date and the override will be silently ignored. Use the organizer's timezone for both sides of the comparison (e.g. `dayjs.tz(slotStartTime, organizerTimeZone).format(...)`).

findings.title: Override boundary check is strict, missing same-instant starts
findings.body: `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` is strict: a slot whose start equals the override end is not filtered, and slots that straddle the override end (e.g. override 14:00–18:00, slot 17:30–18:30) are also not filtered because there is no check that the slot end is within the override. The check should also require `slotStartTime` not to be after `date.end` (use `isSameOrAfter` or also verify the slot end) and the same boundary issue applies to `date.start` (a slot that begins before the override starts but ends inside it slips through).

findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable ignores override.timeZone, uses caller-supplied organizerTimeZone
findings.body: `dateOverrides` are flattened with `timeZone: availability.timeZone` attached, but `checkIfIsAvailable`'s signature drops that field (type is `{ start: Date; end: Date }[]`) and instead uses the caller-supplied `organizerTimeZone` to compute the UTC offset for `date.start`. If a date override was created in a timezone different from the one currently passed as `organizerTimeZone` (e.g. round-robin where a fixed host's override was stored with one tz and `schedule.timeZone` resolves to another, or DST boundary), the override's intended local time will be misinterpreted, returning the wrong availability.

findings.title: override.start.toString() parsed in server local tz, then re-zoned
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` first stringifies a Date (which embeds the server's local timezone offset) and parses it back, then re-zones. The resulting `utcOffset` depends on the server's TZ rather than being a pure UTC interpretation. On any server not running in UTC the organizer/invitee offset values (and therefore the computed `offset` and the resulting `startTime`/`endTime`) will be wrong. Use `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (or pass the Date directly) before `.tz(...)`.

findings.title: override startTime/endTime computed in UTC, not invitee local time
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + …` produces the hour/minute of the shifted UTC instant, but the surrounding `buildSlots` compares these values to `dayStart` which is in the invitee's local timezone. The result is that for two invitees in different timezones the same `startTime` value yields the same UTC slot, regardless of invitee tz. This is exactly the behavior the PR description claims to fix ("date overrides didn't adjust to different timezones"). The correct computation is the override's start in the invitee's local tz, e.g. `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).hour() * 60 + dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).minute()`.

findings.title: New test asserts same UTC slots for two different invitee timezones
findings.body: The new `scheduleForEventOnADayWithDateOverrideDifferentTimezone` case calls `getSchedule` with `timeZone: "Asia/Dhaka"` and expects the identical UTC slots `[08:30, 09:30, 10:30, 11:30]` as the IST case, with the comment "it should return the same as this is the utc time". The PR description says the fix makes date overrides adjust to the attendee's timezone, so two invitees in materially different timezones (e.g. IST vs America/Los_Angeles) should see different UTC slots. The test as written locks in the pre-fix behavior and will not catch a regression of the stated bug; it also only spans a 30-minute tz difference which doesn't expose the problem at all.
